chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I came to Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: “May Allah make me your ransom, what is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,”
“Then let them complete their prescribed duties (tafath).”

He said: “It is taking the mustache, trimming the nails, and the like of that.” He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, for indeed Zurayḥ al-Muḥāribī narrated to me from you that you said: ‘“Let them complete their prescribed duties” means meeting the Imam, and “and let them fulfill their vows” — those are the rites.’”
He said: “Zurayḥ has spoken the truth, and you have spoken the truth. Indeed, the Qur’an has an outward meaning and an inward meaning, and who can bear what Zurayḥ can bear?”

key_terms.أَخْذُ الشَّارِبِ: Trimming the mustache as part of post-rite grooming.
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكُ: The rites and ritual observances of hajj.
key_terms.بَاطِناً: The inward, esoteric meaning of the Qur'an.
key_terms.تَفَثَهُمْ: The state to be removed after hajj rites; explained here outwardly as grooming duties.
key_terms.ظَاهِراً: The outward, apparent meaning of the Qur'an.
key_terms.قَصُّ الْأَظْفَارِ: Cutting the nails as part of completing tafath.
key_terms.لِقَاءُ الْإِمَامِ: Meeting the Imam, given here as the inward meaning of the verse.
key_terms.نُذُورَهُمْ: Their vows, linked here to the ritual acts.

ai.seo_question: What does “ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ” mean in Shia hadith interpretation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about completing tafath in hajj with both an outward and inward meaning. Outwardly, it refers to acts of grooming such as trimming the mustache and cutting the nails, while inwardly it refers to meeting the Imam. The narration highlights the Shia principle that the Qur'an possesses both zahir and batin meanings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3036 - In a narration from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
"I came to Abu Abdullah (as) and asked, 'May I be your ransom, what is the meaning of Allah’s (swt) saying: "Then let them complete their prescribed duties ('tafath')..."?' (Surah Al-Hajj 22:29)
Imam (as) replied: 'It refers to trimming the mustache, cutting the nails, and similar actions.'
I then said: 'May I be your ransom, but Zarih al-Muharibi narrated to me from you that you said:
"Let them complete their prescribed duties ('tafath')" means meeting the Imam, and "fulfill their vows" refers to fulfilling the rituals.'
Imam (as) said: Zarih has spoken the truth, and so have you. Verily, the Qur'an has an apparent meaning and a hidden meaning. And not everyone can bear what Zarih can bear.'"
